persons.name: Henry S Handy

occupation.note: No source in this pass's evidence records an occupation for this person. A poll list, a tax list, a muster roll and a baptismal entry each print a name and no trade, and where a later directory prints one it is a trade of 1843 — T-0633 is the rule for back-projecting that, and this pass does not have it.

persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from death_notice, newspaper_1833_1835. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 18 March 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “HANDY HENRY S”, 1835-06-27 to 1835-09-10: 2 federal land entries — SE sec 14 T38N R14E; W2SW sec 22 T38N R14E, 240.00 acres stated in all, for $300.00 (ls0611, ls0636). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: HANDY HENRY S matches Henry S Handy: the forename names Henry S Handy of the 2 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

merge_ruling.for_merge: The town documents one Handy, a mason, from Andreas; Henry S. Handy is in the Democrat and Fergus's 1843 death notices. A 'Major Handy' and a Henry S. Handy may well be the same man under a militia title.
merge_ruling.against_merge: 'Major Handy' prints no forename at all. Surname-plus-a-title is the refusal data/research/newspapers/identity.json has ratified since the press pass, and this pass does not make an exception to it. Refused by rule.

roles.note: PRINTED AGAINST THIS NAME IN THE 1833-1835 PRESS and carried here from the newspaper gazetteer (T-1254, by tools/derive_resident_roles.py). The gazetteer holds its trades on the PERSON record and not on a single issue, so the bound is the run of this person's own dated mentions, 1834-03-18 to 1834-03-25, and the grade is `inferred`: the paper printed the trade, and the resident programme's identity rule tied the printing to this card. The scene date falls outside that run, so this role does not stand in the 1835 view.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'Henry' is read as male because 1 person in this layer whose sex a source records bears it (lampman_henry_s), and it stands in the yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as '1846' and the age as 'a. 42'. An age of 42 completed years means at least 42 and less than 43, so the birth falls between 1803-01-02 and 1804-12-31: the birth year is 1803 or 1804. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "Handy, Maj. Henry S., contractor, died, Bayfield, Mich., 1846, a. 42.", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
